pages.title: Upper Air | Atlas
pages.visible_text: Debrecen, Hungary - 2026-07-27 to 2026-07-29 Upper Air Model-derived vertical structure over Debrecen: thermodynamics, wind shear, and the evolution of moisture and wind through the full 72-hour report. Model Skew-T i Temperature and dew point rise through decreasing pressure, with a separate wind profile and stability indices. Close temperature and dew-point traces mark moist layers; strong temperature change with height indicates steep lapse rates. Model-derived near Debrecen; this is not an observed radiosonde. Hodograph i The curve traces horizontal wind components with height; colors show kilometres above the lowest model level. A longer or more strongly curved path indicates greater speed shear or directional turning. Bulk-shear values summarize the 0-1, 0-3, and 0-6 km layers. Model-derived near Debrecen; this is not an observed radiosonde. Time-Pressure Curtain i Time runs left to right and pressure decreases upward. Use the plot menu to switch between relative humidity, temperature anomaly by level, and wind speed; surface pressure and precipitation remain below for timing context. A Debrecen-specific time-pressure diagnostic, adapted from a Hovmoller layout without implying spatial longitude or latitude coverage.

pages.title: Weather | Atlas
pages.visible_text: Debrecen, Hungary - 2026-07-27 to 2026-07-29 Surface Weather Four focused diagnostics for wind direction, pressure evolution, near-surface moisture, and solar timing. Wind Rose i Spokes point toward the direction the wind came from. Longer spokes mean that direction occurred more often, and stacked colors divide observations into wind-speed ranges. Pressure Tendency i The line is sea-level pressure; tendency marks the six-hour change. Rapid falls often precede active systems, while sharp rises commonly follow a front or strengthening high pressure. Temperature-Dew Point Spread i A small gap between temperature and dew point indicates moist air near saturation. Shaded periods mark especially small spreads and therefore elevated fog, low-cloud, or condensation potential. Solar Diurnal Curves i Each colored line is one local day. Compare its peak, width, and interruptions with the historical median curve to separate clear, cloudy, and intermittently shaded periods.
